The '''Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies''' ('''ASARB''') is an American non-profit organization that brings together [[statistician]]s from various [[religious denomination|religious group]]s in the United States, with the aim of compiling accurate statistics regarding all such groups. It was established in 1935 and is based in [[Lenexa]], [[Kansas]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.asarb.org/about.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20070717205921/http://www.asarb.org/about.html |archive-date=July 17, 2007 |title=About Us |date=April 23, 2007 |publisher=Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies |access-date=February 19, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.guidestar.org/profile/22-2786373 |title=Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies  |website=GuideStar  |language=en |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> Since 1990, it has sponsored the US Religion Census, a national survey of Americans' religious beliefs conducted independently of, but at the same time as, the [[United States Census]]. This survey had previously been conducted by the [[National Council of Churches]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.usreligioncensus.org/ |title=U.S. Religion Census, 1952 to 2010 |website=U.S. Religion Census |publisher=Association of Statisticians of American Religious Bodies |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Finke |first1=Roger |author1-link=Roger Finke |last2=Bader |first2=Christopher D. |year=2011 |chapter=Data and Directions for Research in the Economics of Religion |editor-last=McCleary |editor-first=Rachel M. |editor-link=Rachel McCleary |title=The Oxford Handbook of the Economics of Religion |location=New York |publisher=Oxford University Press |doi=10.1093/oxfordhb/9780195390049.013.0018 |isbn=978-0-19-978128-7 |page=351}}</ref> It has become increasingly important since the US Census stopped asking Americans about their religion after [[World War II]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Harrison |first=Judy |date=May 18, 2012 |title=Got Faith? Maine the Least-Religious State in the Nation |url=http://bangordailynews.com/2012/05/18/religion/got-faith-maine-the-least-religious-state-in-the-nation/ |work=Bangor Daily News |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref>
